title: Donation swap (sUSDS -> waUSDC) is executed with limitRaw=0 and only the post-unwrap USDC is slippage-checked, enabling sandwich extraction inside the same unlock callback
description:
Inside unlockCallback the donation phase performs `IBalancerVault.swap(VaultSwapParams({ ..., amountGivenRaw: donationSUSDS, limitRaw: 0, ... }))` — i.e., it accepts any non-zero amount of waUSDC out. The slippage gate is moved to a single `require(usdcReceived >= minUSDC)` after `IERC4626(waUsdc).redeem(...)`. This conflates two independent slippage surfaces into one:

1. Spot price of sUSDS/waUSDC on the Balancer V3 pool at execution time (sandwichable). This determines waUsdcReceived.
2. waUSDC <> USDC redemption rate on the Aave wrapper (the ERC4626 share-to-asset ratio). This determines usdcReceived from waUsdcReceived.

Because `limitRaw` is zero, the pooler effectively can only protect against a combined drop. If the swap leg is sandwiched while the waUSDC->USDC rate stays put (which it does — Aave waUSDC's ERC4626 rate updates only as Aave interest accrues and is therefore effectively constant within a block), then any sandwich on the swap leg directly reduces the USDC eventually delivered to batchMinter by the price-impact percentage of the front-run/back-run. The caller's `minUSDC` is the only safety net; if the pooler bot computed it off-chain from a stale quote and used 99% slippage, an attacker who can move the sUSDS/waUSDC pool by 1.1% (e.g., on a thin pool or with a flashloan) will profit.

Worse, the swap and the addLiquidity execute in the SAME unlock callback. An attacker who is the same entity controlling the pool state across the unlock-window can move the sUSDS/waUSDC pool ahead of the swap, then the sUSDS/phUSD pool ahead of the addLiquidity, with a single bundled transaction. There is no per-leg slippage cap, no deadline, and limitRaw is hard-coded to zero in the source (not even configurable by the caller).
exploit_path:
Setup: BalancerPoolerV2 holds X sUSDS. batchDonationSize = 50 means donationSUSDS = X/2 will flow through the swap.

Attack:
1. MEV bot observes pool(minBPT, minUSDC) in the mempool. minUSDC is, by design, calibrated against the joint swap+unwrap, but the pooler can only guess at the joint slippage and is forced to set it relatively loose because of the two-stage uncertainty.
2. Bundle:
   a. Frontrun: flashloan sUSDS, swap sUSDS -> waUSDC on the sUSDS/waUSDC pool (limitRaw=0 not relevant — attacker controls his own swap). This pushes waUSDC's price (per sUSDS) down on the pool.
   b. pool() executes. The donation swap goes through at the worse price. Because limitRaw=0, even an aggressive sandwich does not trigger a revert here. The pool emits some waUsdcReceived, well below what an unsandwiched swap would yield.
   c. Unwrap waUSDC -> USDC. The Aave ERC4626 redeem rate is fixed in-block, so usdcReceived = waUsdcReceived * sharePrice. usdcReceived is below `minUSDC` only if the pooler set minUSDC tight relative to actual mainnet conditions; in practice the pooler bot will set it loose enough that the call still succeeds.
   d. Backrun: swap waUSDC -> sUSDS on the same pool, repaying the flashloan and pocketing the spread.
3. The pooler's batchMinter receives less USDC; the MEV bot pockets the difference.

Profit estimate: For a donationSUSDS of $50k against a $3M-deep sUSDS/waUSDC pool with 0.04% fee, a 100bps sandwich extracts roughly $300-$500 per pool() call after gas. Repeated weekly: ~$15k-$25k/year leaked to MEV, all from yield earmarked for batchMinter.

Additionally, because the swap and addLiquidity occur in the SAME unlock callback (and thus same tx), a single MEV bundle can sandwich both legs simultaneously, compounding the extraction described in ECON-RAW-001 with the donation-swap extraction here.
mainnet_realism: Balancer V3 sUSDS/waUSDC Aave-Boosted pools exist on mainnet (the Sky/Aave integration). Pool depth varies; smaller boosted pools (<$5M TVL) regularly carry >50bps slippage on $50k trades. The fee tier on Aave-boosted stable pools is typically 0.04-0.10%, which does NOT protect joiners against sandwiches where the searcher pays the fee on both legs but the joiner pays it on one leg of the joint position. waUSDC (Aave wrapped USDC) is a standard ERC4626 with negligible deviation from its share price during a single block — so the assumption that `usdcReceived >= minUSDC` covers swap-leg slippage is mainnet-incorrect: the swap leg can be sandwiched freely as long as the combined output clears minUSDC, and any pooler bot setting a loose minUSDC (necessary because of the joint-uncertainty) hands the spread to MEV.
recommendation: Replace `limitRaw: 0` with a caller-supplied per-leg slippage cap, e.g., add a `minWaUsdc` parameter to `pool()` (or compute it on-chain via IBalancerRouter.querySwapSingleTokenExactIn immediately before the swap and apply a tight tolerance). Also enforce that the donation swap and addLiquidity occur in separate transactions so they cannot both be sandwiched in a single MEV bundle — alternatively, gate `pool()` behind a private mempool / Flashbots-Protect endpoint and require the pooler bot to submit through it. Add a `deadline` parameter to all of `pool()` and revert if `block.timestamp > deadline`. Document that the pooler operator MUST set `minUSDC` and the new `minWaUsdc` based on a fresh on-chain query and not on a precomputed estimate.
severity_rationale: Downgraded from initial High guess to Medium. Hard-coded `limitRaw: 0` on the donation swap genuinely conflates two slippage surfaces into one, leaving the swap leg unprotected per-leg. The amplification when combined with same-tx addLiquidity sandwich (ECON-RAW-001) is real. However, like ECON-RAW-001, the function is callable only via onlyAuthorizedPooler — the at-risk assets are protocol-earmarked yield (USDC delivered to batchMinter), not user-held funds. The attack requires the operator bot to broadcast publicly (no private-relay) and to set minUSDC sufficiently loose that combined-swap-plus-unwrap slippage still passes. Per C4, this is a value leak with stated assumptions (public mempool submission + loose operator-set minUSDC). It impairs the protocol's donation/batch-minter funding stream — protocol availability/function impact — fitting Medium. Not High because the attack path requires external operator-configuration assumptions, not pure on-chain conditions.
poc_notes: Forked mainnet (latest) using real Balancer V3 Vault 0xbA1333..., Router 0xAE563E..., real boosted stable pool 0x0B65A4... (sUSDS/waEthUSDC/waEthUSDT), real Permit2 0x000000...22D473. No AMM mocking. Headline: at 500 sUSDS attack size, USDC delivered to batchMinter drops from 219.0 USDC -> 139.1 USDC (36.51% loss, ~$79.97 victim loss); attacker recovers 570.99 sUSDS for 500 sUSDS input (~$77.87 attacker profit). Size sweep test shows profitability threshold sits near 500 sUSDS at this block — smaller sizes are unprofitable for the attacker but still leak value from the victim. Includes a direct proof test (test_econ_raw_002_swap_leg_accepts_arbitrarily_bad_rate) showing pool() succeeds with minUSDC=1 even after the curve is pushed by a 400 sUSDS dump — confirms limitRaw=0 is the structural gap.
rejection_reason: The finding mischaracterises the post-unwrap `minUSDC` check as "conflating" two slippage surfaces. Because the waUSDC->USDC unwrap rate (Aave ERC4626 convertToAssets) is deterministic and fixed within a block, the relationship `usdcReceived = waUsdcReceived * R(block)` means a single `minUSDC` floor is algebraically equivalent to a per-leg `minWaUsdc` / `limitRaw` cap — it aggregates the two legs into one bound rather than weakening protection. The recommended fix (expose `minWaUsdc`) adds nothing the operator doesn't already control via `minUSDC`. The "limitRaw=0 is a structural gap" PoC clears the check by setting `minUSDC=1`, which is tautological: any slippage parameter set to a no-op disables its check. Once the conflation framing is dropped, the finding reduces to the same content as the already-rejected M-01 — operator broadcasts publicly with a loose slippage parameter — which is a C4-invalid operational-misconfiguration concern, not a code bug.
